references.text: A direct parallel listing the same sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram
Traces the lineage from Shem through Arphaxad to Abram, thus expanding on one of the sons mentioned in Genesis 10:22
Noah's blessing over Shem, providing theological background for Shem's lineage in Genesis 10:22
Mentions both Elam and Asshur among the nations where the Lord will gather Israel's remnant, showing the further role of these nations in biblical history
A prophecy against Elam, one of the nations descended from Shem, illustrating Elam's role in God's plan
Names Elam as a military power, highlighting the historical significance of this nation descended from Shem
Luke confirms Arphaxad's role as Shem's son and shows the continuity of salvation history from the flood to Christ.
Continues the account of Arphaxad by specifying the time of birth and the age of Shem.
Expands the picture of Shem's family by noting that he had more children after Arphaxad.
Creates a contrast and parallel by showing Ham's sons, who are brothers to Shem's sons.
Confirms the list of Ham's sons and strengthens the parallel to Shem's sons.
Shows the historical development of Elam, the first son of Shem, into a distinct nation.
Summarizes the purpose of the list by explaining the dispersion according to clans, languages and lands.
Confirms the same lineage (Shem-Arphaxad-Shelah) in a shorter overview.
Places Shem's sons in context by identifying Shem as one of Noah's three sons.
